goal: Implement SPADE (Structured Pruning and Adaptive Distillation for Efficient LLM-TTS, arXiv:2509.20802, ICASSP 2026) as a runnable research codebase: WER-based layer importance (WLI) pruning plus adaptive multi-level knowledge distillation (Skew-KL logits, latent/attention/embedding MSE, dynamic layer matching) for LLM-TTS backbones.

requirement_alignment.source: Derived from user request ('implement this repo's idea'), the empty README title (SPADE: Structured Pruning and Adaptive Distillation for Efficient LLM-TTS), and the full paper text (arXiv 2509.20802v3) + DistiLLM reference implementation. No blocking question asked because the paper is an unambiguous spec and the user explicitly asked to implement directly.
requirement_alignment.goal: Self-contained, runnable implementation of SPADE: train an LLM-TTS teacher, compute WER-based layer importance, prune low-importance layers, recover via adaptive multi-level distillation, evaluate WER/efficiency.
non_goals: Full reproduction of the paper's CosyVoice 2 / LLaSA benchmarks (requires multi-GPU + LibriHeavy/LibriTTS-scale corpora)
Quantization / other compression methods (out of SPADE scope)
user_visible_behavior: CLI commands: train teacher, compute WLI + prune, distill pruned student, evaluate, and one-command end-to-end pipeline
Built-in synthetic speech-codec benchmark so the whole pipeline runs end-to-end in minutes on available hardware
Real-data hooks: EnCodec-style discrete-audio token dataset loader and optional Whisper-based WER scorer
README documenting method, usage, configs, and extension points (CosyVoice 2 / LLaSA)
constraints: Minimal external dependencies (torch, numpy, pyyaml, tqdm); optional whisper/torchaudio for real-audio evaluation
Tests must be fast (small models, synthetic data) and run with pytest
Preserve the single existing README.md content intent (SPADE title) while expanding it
risks: Synthetic codec is a proxy benchmark, not real speech; real-data validation requires the provided adapters and external datasets
WLI requires autoregressive decoding per layer; cost controlled via small eval subset
acceptance_checks: End-to-end smoke pipeline (train tiny teacher -> WLI -> prune -> distill -> evaluate) runs and reports WER + efficiency metrics
README documents method and CLI usage
requirement_alignment.validation_approach: pytest unit tests per module plus an end-to-end smoke test on tiny synthetic configuration
requirement_alignment.first_iteration_scope: Project scaffolding (pyproject, package skeleton, .gitignore) + minimal GPT-style LLM-TTS backbone + text tokenizer + synthetic speech-codec data + unit tests
follow_up_iterations: WLI pruning module + cosine baseline + tests
Adaptive distillation (losses + dynamic matching + trainer) + tests
CLI wiring (train/prune/distill/evaluate/pipeline), README, end-to-end smoke test, PR
assumptions: User wants a faithful, runnable implementation of the paper's method rather than a full benchmark reproduction
Skew KL uses DistiLLM's skewed-forward-KL formulation (mixed = beta*p + (1-beta)*q, KL(p||mixed), beta=0.1) as in the referenced implementation
Dynamic layer matching: student layer n distills from teacher layer r_{n+1}-1 (last layer before the next retained layer); last student layer distills from the final teacher layer
WLI: leave-one-out layer removal measured on a small evaluation subset with a WER scorer; prune bottom-k, force-keep first and last layer
GitHub issues/PRs on the private ml-inory/SPADE repo are authorized (gh authenticated as repo owner ml-inory)
open_questions: Whether to later add native CosyVoice 2 / LLaSA integration beyond generic HF-transformer hooks (can be a follow-up iteration)

issues.title: feat[1]: Project scaffolding, LLM-TTS backbone, and synthetic codec data
acceptance_checks: pyproject.toml, .gitignore, and spade/ package skeleton exist with minimal dependencies
spade/models/llm_tts.py provides a configurable autoregressive LLM-TTS backbone returning logits + hidden states + attention maps
spade/data/ provides character tokenizer and synthetic speech-codec dataset decodable back to text
Model forward/generation and data pipeline have passing pytest unit tests

issues.title: feat[2]: WER-based layer importance (WLI) pruning + cosine baseline
acceptance_checks: spade/pruning/ provides compute_wli (leave-one-out WER per layer), compute_cli (mean cosine distance between layer input/output), and layer selection/pruning utilities
Backbone supports temporarily disabling blocks (leave-one-out) and pruning returns a new student model whose retained blocks copy teacher weights
WER scorer abstraction: built-in token-codec scorer decoding generated codes to text; optional Whisper-based scorer for real audio
Pruning + selection + scorer have passing pytest tests

issues.title: feat[3]: Adaptive multi-level distillation (Skew-KL losses, dynamic layer matching, trainer)
acceptance_checks: spade/distill/losses.py provides CE, Skew KL (DistiLLM forward/reverse, masked), latent/attention/embedding MSE, and the SPADE composite loss (alpha=0.25 default)
spade/distill/matching.py provides dynamic teacher-layer targets (last layer before next retained; final layer for the last student layer) and the static ablation
spade/distill/trainer.py trains the student against a frozen teacher with the composite loss and returns per-component metrics
Losses, matching, and trainer have passing pytest tests (including teacher frozen / student updated)

rounds.test_summary: 11 passed (model forward/generation/causality/multi-codebook, codec roundtrip, dataset collation, WER basics)
rounds.implementation_summary: Created the spade package with a GPT-style LLM-TTS backbone (causal attention + residual blocks + LM heads, exposing hidden states/attention maps/embedding outputs for distillation) and a data layer with a character tokenizer, an invertible context-dependent synthetic speech codec, and a dataset/collator.
rounds.gate_rationale: Tests passed; assumed user wants the full SPADE implementation (pruning + distillation + CLI + PR) rather than stopping after scaffolding. Recorded as an assumption; user can redirect at any time.

rounds.test_summary: 18 passed (WLI leave-one-out + restore, layer selection with boundary forcing, weight-copy pruning, CLI computation, token-codec WER scorer)
rounds.implementation_summary: Implemented WER-based layer importance (leave-one-out layer bypass scored with WER), cosine-based layer importance baseline, top-k layer selection with optional first/last retention, and a prune_layers utility that builds the student by copying retained teacher blocks. Added TokenCodecWERScorer (generated codes -> text -> WER) and WhisperWERScorer for the real-audio path, plus efficiency metrics.

rounds.test_summary: 27 passed (skew-KL forward/reverse/masking, MSE losses, composite weights, dynamic/static matching, distill loss components, trainer updates student and freezes teacher, ablation flags)
rounds.implementation_summary: Implemented the paper's composite distillation loss (alpha*CE + (1-alpha)/4 * (skew-KL logit + latent MSE + attention MSE + embedding MSE), alpha=0.25) with DistiLLM's skew KL (beta=0.1, forward/reverse), dynamic teacher-layer matching (target = last teacher layer before the next retained layer) plus static ablation, and a DistillTrainer that freezes the teacher and returns per-component metrics.
